items.headline: Anthropic completes IPO, begins trading on Nasdaq as ANT
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its $70-$78 range, and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19, in one of the largest tech listings on record. The debut tests investor appetite for AI-lab economics amid growing scrutiny of circular financing deals among frontier labs.

items.headline: Anthropic's Amodei recommits to "pacing" AI development at Nasdaq bell
items.summary: At Anthropic's Nasdaq opening-bell ceremony marking its public debut, CEO Dario Amodei reiterated the company's stated commitment to developing AI deliberately rather than racing ahead, regardless of competitive or political pressure. The remarks underscore the tension between Anthropic's safety-focused positioning and its new status as a public, growth-driven company.

items.headline: Meta's AI agent Muse reportedly mixing up conversations, exposing private data
items.summary: Meta employees have raised internal concerns that the company's AI agent Muse has been crossing conversations between different user accounts, potentially exposing private data, according to a Reuters report. A Meta spokesperson defended the issue as part of normal product-development testing.

items.headline: Google gives Gemini the ability to take over your Mac
items.summary: Google added computer-use capability to its Gemini app on macOS, letting the assistant perform multi-step tasks on a user's behalf while pausing for approval before key actions. The feature requires a paid Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription and extends the ongoing push by major AI labs into autonomous desktop agents.

items.headline: US tightens AI chip export rules to close China's overseas data-center loophole
items.summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule on November 16 aimed at preventing Chinese firms from accessing advanced American chips through overseas cloud data centers. China's Commerce Ministry said on November 17 it firmly opposes the move and warned of retaliatory measures.

items.headline: CoreWeave signs multi-year cloud deal to power Wayve's self-driving AI training
items.summary: Autonomous-driving startup Wayve will train, evaluate and simulate its mapless "AI Driver" foundation models on CoreWeave's cloud using Nvidia Blackwell GPUs under a new multi-year agreement. The deal expands Wayve's compute capacity as it pushes toward hardware-agnostic self-driving systems for automakers and fleet operators.

items.headline: Munich starts autonomous bus trial with real passengers
items.summary: MAN Truck & Bus and transit operator MVG began carrying registered test passengers on a 12-metre autonomous electric bus on Munich route 178 starting November 17, part of the MINGA research project monitored by the Technical University of Munich. The bus still runs as an addition to scheduled service rather than a replacement, with trials set to continue until mid-2027.

items.headline: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubles accuracy in predicting disease-linked DNA variants
items.summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how DNA variants affect specific human cell types rather than averaged tissue samples, identifying nearly twice as many expression-altering variants as its predecessor. The model is free for academic research via API but not yet validated for clinical or diagnostic use.

items.headline: MIT-developed AI model roughly doubles reliability of 2-6 week weather forecasts
items.summary: Researchers led by MIT's Judah Cohen built an AI postprocessing layer that learns from a forecasting system's historical errors to sharpen subseasonal predictions, doubling forecast reliability for the two-to-six-week range when applied to ECMWF's system. The approach reportedly flagged a severe US cold snap and a major blizzard weeks ahead of traditional long-range models.
